title: Introduce json-schema response_format with strict validation and clearer error codes
author: Priya Varma
description: Motivation: provide first-class JSON Schema support on the API surface so service owners can declare expected structured outputs and get deterministic validation and helpful errors. This change adds a new response_format option 'json_schema' (OpenAI-compat wrapper), a strict validation mode that causes returns to fail fast when the model output does not conform, best-effort auto-correction attempts in streaming mode, and structured error codes for client consumption. Scope: API/compat layer, streaming runtime hooks, validation util, CLI validation, tests, and docs. Checklist: - Implement response_format parsing and extension in openai_compat adapter - Add streaming validator that ingests token stream and validates partial JSON where possible - Implement post-response validation with error codes: VALIDATION_FAILED, AUTO_CORRECTED, STRICT_VIOLATION - Wire strict=true behavior to set HTTP 422 + structured error payload - Add on-by-default for SDK preview opt-in; documented in docs/api/response_format.md - Tests and fuzz harness for schema edge cases - Backwards-compatible: default behavior remains text/json fallback Implementation notes: The adapter accepts response_format:{type:'json_schema',schema:<JSON Schema as string>,strict:<bool>} or the OpenAI-style top-level 'response_format' field. Streaming validator maintains a partial parse buffer and runs incremental validation against permissive subset of the schema to provide early hints; when strict=true we abort the request and return structured error as soon as the validator detects an irrecoverable mismatch. For non-strict mode we return the original output with attached validation.report and, when confidence is high, an AUTO_CORRECTED variant produced by the repair module. Error payload: {error_code, message, schema_path, example_corrections}. Backwards compat: if the client provides an OpenAI 'response_format' string we map it to our internal structure; if unknown, we fall back to legacy behavior. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind api.json_schema_support; staged canary across regional routing; telemetry added to monitor strict failures. Related: ENG-1143 tracks performance budget for streaming validation, ENG-1187 tracks docs and SDK changes. Tests: unit tests in tests/test_json_schema.py, integration in perf-canary suite. CI: lint, unit, integration (mock runtime), and e2e in canary passed locally. See files_changed for details and example snippets.

streaming: incremental validator and buffer management
validation: repair module and structured error types
docs: response_format examples and migration guide
tests: json schema unit & integration coverage
ci: add fuzz harness for schema edge cases

review_comments: Evan Li: Please add a note about performance impact on 1kRPS workloads; incremental validator looks good but we need microbenchmarks. Author: Added microbenchmark numbers to streaming_validator and a caveat in rollout.

Sofia Martinez: For strict=true, how do we expose schema_path to clients securely? Author: We only expose a trimmed schema_path (max depth 6) and redact $ref contents; updated error payload accordingly.

Marcus Chen: Can AUTO_CORRECTED be abused to hide model regressions? Author: AUTO_CORRECTED returns a 'correction_score' and is only allowed in non-strict mode; added telemetry and opt-in flag in SDK.
release_notes: - New response_format type: json_schema — allows servers to validate and enforce JSON schema on model outputs. - Added strict mode: when enabled, non-conforming outputs return 422 with structured error codes. - Streaming validator: early detection and best-effort corrections in non-strict mode. - SDKs updated to accept response_format in OpenAI-compat params. See docs/api/response_format.md for migration guidance.
example_error: HTTP 422 body: {"error_code":"STRICT_VIOLATION","message":"output did not satisfy schema: missing required property 'order_id'","schema_path":"#/required/0","example_corrections":["{\"order_id\":\"<id>\"}"]}
notes: This PR introduces a new capability; follow-on work includes SDK defaulting UX, RBAC control for schema features, and sampling policy for telemetry to avoid PII leaks.
